notices.trigger: At the time of contracting, for a licensed residential builder, remodeler or roofer
notices.format: Placed on the contracting document immediately before the space for the purchaser's signature, in bold and conspicuous type larger than the rest of the contract
notices.support: This disclosure shall be placed on the contracting document immediately before the space reserved on the document for the signature of the purchaser, shall be in bold and conspicuous type with a font size larger than the font appearing on the remainder of the contract
notices.summary_row: General liability insurance disclosure: exact words, placement, type size
notices.hold_reason: The block also contains Rule 1.2 (the job-site permit sign), which is not contract text, and the Board's rule gives the sentence only in the "I DO carry" form with blanks for insurer and policy number; there is no official wording for a contractor who does not carry insurance.

notices.format: Under the conspicuous caption BUYER'S RIGHT TO CANCEL; no type size stated; the Federal Trade Commission form is accepted instead
notices.summary_row: "BUYER'S RIGHT TO CANCEL" statement (credit sales at the home)

changes.new: Until midnight on the third business day after the buyer signs; business day is not defined. Until the seller gives the statement, the buyer may cancel by any means. The state statement lets the seller keep up to 5 percent of the cash price, which the federal rule does not allow, so the federal form is the safer notice.
changes.support: Day count. "before midnight on the third business day after you sign this agreement". The definitions section (75-66-1) has two terms only and does not define "business day".

unsure: MS-insurance: the rule makes every licensed residential builder, remodeler or roofer print the disclosure, so it should print for every licensed contract, but the block mixes in Rule 1.2 and has no variant for an uninsured contractor, so it is held.

MS-cancel-credit: the state text is VERBATIM-SECONDARY (Justia mirror), so it cannot be loaded; also credit versus cash sale is not something the builder knows, and the 5 percent retention wording conflicts with the federal full refund.
mirror_source left false: the insurance disclosure comes from the Board's own publication, only the cancellation chapter comes from a mirror.
